Along the eastern side of the Slate Range the sequence typically has a several meter thick interbeds of debris flow deposits and conglomerate; locally separated out as volcanic debris flow deposits (Nmv). title: marble
description: Light gray ductilely deformed marble. In the northern portion of the map area it occurs in a set of duplicated thrust horses and as pods of mylonitic marble along the Argus-Sterling thrust, where it is about 15 m thick. This marble is thicker in Water Canyon where it is ~200 m thick with a basal lenticular unit of gray marble ~25 m thick, overlain by tan-weathering, laminated calcsilcate-hornfels and thin-bedded marble. Southeast of Fish Canyon in Slate Range, this marble occurs in a set of thrusts that duplicate this unit with the Conglomerate Mesa Formation(?).

These folds in the flow foliation of basaltic lava are interpreted to be where the lavas flowed over fault scarps. description: Volcanic debris flow deposits occurs throughout the area above the white pyroclastic deposits and below the Miocene intermediate composition lava flows. Most of these units are poorly sorted breccias with angular to subangular clasts but at several localities these breccias grade upward into a well-bedded conglomerate of the same dacitic clast types. title: Bird Spring Formation
description: Medium gray limestone and silty limestone and metamorphosed equivalents exposed in the upper part of the Argus-Sterling thrust fault in the northern Slate Range. It occurs stratigraphically above the Mississippian Santa Rosa Hills Limestone and is overthrust by tectonized marble. The exposed thickness is 150 m with a lower half of medium to dark gray micritic limestone, tan-weathering silty or argillaceous limestone and graded echinodermal limestone beds (Stone, 1984). The upper half is similar but is dominated by silty argillaceous limestone. Graded beds indicate this unit is the Keeler Canyon Formation and not of the time-equivalent Bird Spring Formation (Stone, 1984). In the Slate Range, there are two thrust slices: the structurally lower slice is monotonous medium gray limestone with pervasively foliated tremolitic marble and a gray meta-limestone with preserved crinoids (Moore, 1976) and 1–2 cm chert nodules (i.e., ‘golfball’ member of lower Keeler Canyon Formation). title: mylonite of felsic
description: Blue-gray to white mylonite to mylonitic schist and gneiss. The protolith was likely a felsic Jurassic volcanic rock (Moore, 1976). The original textures have been obliterated by distributed shear and metamorphism during top to the northeast thrust-sense movement. These rocks occur in a deformation zone between hanging wall plutonic rocks and footwall Mesozoic metasedimentary and metavolcanic rocks of the Argus-Sterling thrust fault, part of the Jurassic Eastern California thrust system (Dunne and Walker, 2004).

title: Jvs
description: Dark-colored meta-siltstone, sandstone, conglomerate, and ignimbrite. The conglomerate units are distinctive with rounded felsic volcanic clasts in a dark blue-colored, fine-grained sandstone matrix (matrix supported). Felsic meta-ignimbrites with preserved eutaxitic textures are well exposed just southeast of Shepherd Canyon, structurally below the dark blue conglomerate. The age of this unit is interpreted to be Late Jurassic based similar volcanic rocks in the region (Dunne et al., 1998; Dunne and Walker, 2004).

title: green-altered basal basalt
description: A basalt lava flow is often present at the base of the Miocene volcanic section, except at locations with older rhyolitic lava domes (in canyons north of Fish Canyon in the eastern Slate Range) where there are no basalt flows. Most of these basalts are greenish black or have green “spots” because on extensive hydrous alteration to celadonite(?). The thickest section of this unit occurs along the eastern Slate Range north of Fish Canyon, where it is over 10 m thick. This thick section also has strong cooling entablature, which gives the outcrop an aspect of apparent bedding. description: Local, mappable bodies of porphyritic plagioclase lath andesite lava flows. One red-colored andesite lava flow occurs in the mouth of Millspaugh Canyon below the white pyroclastic unit. title: rhyolite dome
description: A few exposures of rhyolitic lava occur at the base of the Miocene volcanic section. These lava flows and domes occur in several canyons north of Fish Canyon in the Slate Range. The lava dome has steeply-dipping flow foliations and thick lava flows (20–30 m) relative to length. The lava flows have flow foliation and basal and upper breccia zones. The color ranges from black glass to purple and gray aphanitic lava. These lava flows and lava domes appear to have been topographic highs that subsequent volcanic rocks were deposited around with buttress unconformities. title: Bird Spring Formation
description: Gray marble, with local chert and tremolitic marble, locally with abundant epidote (Moore, 1976; Stone, 1984). These are thick-bedded, cherty limestones where there are lower grades of metamorphism (Stone, 1984). These beds weather to dark blue to black colored surfaces. This unit is allochthonous in the southeastern Argus Range and the northern Slate Range (Stone, 1984). This unit is locally intensely brecciated, altered, and metamorphosed (Stone, 1984). title: Perdido Formation
description: Brown-weathering chert in beds and lenses 1–10 cm thick, interbedded with medium gray limestone in 2–20 cm thick beds. Crinoid fragments locally occur in the limestone interbeds (Moore, 1976). This map unit may include a portion of the Tin Mountain Limestone (Moore, 1976).

title: Hunter Mountain quartz monzonite
description: Medium-grained, equigranular quartz monzonite that intrudes sedimentary rocks structurally below the thrust belt in this map area. Chlorite alteration is common in the western portions of this pluton. title: lacustrine limestone
description: Yellow to gray, well-bedded, vuggy lacustrine limestone. These beds overlie Miocene and Pliocene lava flows and locally are deposited as fringing reef-like bodies with buttress unconformities in Panamint Valley near the mouth of Millspaugh Canyon. Mastodon fossils were found in correlative deposits in eastern Shepherd Canyon (Pesci, 1958).

title: washed surface
description: Older sediments with surfaces modified by Pleistocene lakes: numerous paleo-lake shoreline beaches and wave-cut terraces with abundant rounded and polished pebbles and local accumulations of gastropod fossils and tufa. The high-stand beach terrace is at 695 m elevation in Searles Valley. This correlates with members A to B of the Searles Lake Formation (Smith, 2009). The washed surfaces are poorly preserved on the west side of Panamint Valley. title: Independence dike swarm
description: Plagioclase porphyritic diorite. These intrude Triassic to Jurassic metasedimentary rocks and appear to grade into porphyritic diorite dikes. The largest exposure contains strongly porphyritic textures with medium-grained phenocrysts of plagioclase and quartz in an aphanitic white-gray matrix. Moore (1976) interpreted this unit to be a border phase of the Hunter Mountain Quartz Monzonite, but this unit has porphyritic textures similar to the regionally abundant, Late Jurassic Independence dike swarm (Chen and Moore, 1979) and intrudes units interpreted to be Late Jurassic. title: qmz of Anthony Mill
description: Potassium feldspar-bearing porphyritic quartz monzonite named by Moore (1976). This unit is distinctive with large (1–4 cm), red-colored, tabular potassium feldspar phenocrysts in a medium-grained, gray crystalline matrix. Moore (1976) classified this unit as post-tectonic in the Argus Range, but outcrops in the Slate Range show ductile fabrics including steeply-oriented shear zones with north-trending lineations. This rock is petrologically similar to the Late Jurassic (ca. 151 Ma) Manly Peak Quartz Monzonite (Johnson, 1957; Andrew, 2019) that outcrops to the southwest, across Panamint Valley in the Panamint Range. title: syntectonic alaskite
description: Fine-grained alaskite with cataclastic foliation after Moore (1976). This unit occurs in the immediate hanging wall of the Argus-Sterling thrust. Its deformation fabrics are variable from strong foliations to mortar textures and local chlorite metamorphism. A sample from this unit has a U-Pb zircon age of 187 ± 1 Ma (Dunne and Walker, 2004).

title: Maturango Peak quartz monzonite
description: Quartz monzonite with abundant, coarse, pink potassium feldspar phenocrysts (Moore, 1976). This unit has abundant ductile shear fabrics in it and these zones also have abundant green chlorite-rich zones. This rock has a U-Pb zircon age of ca. 160 Ma (Chen and Moore, 1979) from a sample farther north in the Argus Range. Jhm

title: mylonite
description: Green, chlorite-rich mylonite in the Argus Range. The protoliths for this unit are interpreted to be Jurassic plutonic rocks. This has a steep to moderate westward dipping foliation and abundant shallowly-plunging, north-trending lineations. The sense of shear is dextral. This chlorite-grade ductile deformation has been locally reactivated by brittle deformation under oxidizing conditions, with normal-sense movement.

title: meta-andesite
description: Medium to dark gray-green, massive, non-porphyritic rocks with a dioritic or andesitic composition. Moore (1976) interpreted these as andesite flows based on the obvious volcanic features and textures of nearby rocks and reported observations of volcanic breccia and tuff interbeds, neither of which were seen by the current author. Moore (1976) also mapped a fine-grained diorite pluton along this belt of rocks, which has similar mineralogy and textures. These igneous units are grouped together because of a lack of easily visible differences in the field and the strong metamorphism that often obscures definitive protolith interpretation. These are interpreted to be Late Jurassic, similar to rocks found in the nearby southern Slate Range (Dunne and Walker, 2004) and in the southeastern Panamint Range (Andrew, 2002).

title: Copper Queen Canyon Granite

title: quartz monzonite of Isham Canyon
description: Light gray, biotite-bearing, medium-grained, equigranular quartz monzonite. Moore (1976) interpreted this unit to intrude the Stockwell Diorite but the U-Pb zircon age of the quartz monzonite of Isham Canyon is 166 ± 9 Ma (Dunne and Walker, 2004). The sample used for this age analysis is interpreted to have been switched with the sample for the Stockwell Diorite that gave an age of 100 ± 3 Ma. These samples were collected at the same locality and have similar sample labels. Examination of the archived mineral separates indicates a more felsic rock for the younger sample, thus the quartz monzonite of Isham Canyon is Cretaceous.

title: megabreccia of clasts of Johnnie Formation
description: Unsorted, coarse-grained, monolithologic deposit of green-gray, meta-calcsilicates laminated on a centimeter-scale with gray silica-rich layers all of which has a strong ductile deformation fabric. Clasts range from 1–2 m angular boulders to cobble and pebble sizes. These clasts are correlated to the Neoproterozoic Johnnie Formation present in the western Panamint Range (Andrew and Walker, 2009), although they may correlate to the middle member of the Noonday Dolomite in the Panamint Range.

title: hornblende diorite of Goler Wash
description: Diorite that is interpreted to be a border phase of the Hunter Mountain quartz monzonite (Moore, 1976). This unit contains plagioclase and pyroxene phenocrysts.

title: meta-siltstone
description: Epidote quartz hornfels of siltstone protoliths. The color of this rock varies from bright green to reddish gray and most exposures have abundant fractures, possibly due to the massive texture and the close proximity of the thrust belt. This unit is structurally overlain by meta-andesite mylonites.

title: granite of Argus Peak
description: Light gray, medium to coarse-grained, equigranular granite that weathers into large pinnacle shapes. Correlated to regional isolated plutons of undeformed granitic rocks with Late Cretaceous ages (e.g., 70 Ma Hall Canyon Granite in the western Panamint Range [Mahood et al., 1996]).

title: volcanic debrid flow deposit
description: Volcanic debris flow deposits occurs throughout the area above the white pyroclastic deposits and below the Miocene intermediate composition lava flows. These rock units are grayish-tan deposits of dacitic lava clasts and probably represent lahar deposits, although there is no known source area. Most of these units are poorly sorted breccias with angular to subangular clasts but at several localities these breccias grade upward into a well-bedded conglomerate of the same dacitic clast types. title: Stockwell diorite
description: Plagioclase porphyritic diorite. These intrude Triassic to Jurassic metasedimentary rocks and appear to grade into porphyritic diorite dikes. The largest exposure contains strongly porphyritic textures with medium-grained phenocrysts of plagioclase and quartz in an aphanitic white-gray matrix. Moore (1976) interpreted this unit to be a border phase of the Hunter Mountain Quartz Monzonite, but this unit has porphyritic textures similar to the regionally abundant, Late Jurassic Independence dike swarm (Chen and Moore, 1979) and intrudes units interpreted to be Late Jurassic.
